newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, U.S. in focus.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip on profit-taking, U.S. in focus.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Thursday, hit by profit-taking and uncertainty about U.S. forward trends, with dealers seeing levels holding.

"The FOMC inaction on U.S. rates has caused some uncertainty in the market, which is solidly focused on Wall Street and upcoming American data. We should see current levels holding on Friday depending on U.S. trends," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.61 point down at 165.92, while the KFX June future fell 2.40 point to 165.75 with 486 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
A.P.Moeller paper falls hit the index, with Danisco and GN Store Nord, two of the few KFX papers to make any advances, compensating.
Danisco closed three crowns higher at 396 while GN Store Nord ended the day 10.7 crowns up at 680.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.007 billion crowns.
